Do not replace it with a start event, a subprocess, or an intermediate event unless the description states a message, a separately defined process, or an occurrence the process waits for. Do not drop the action from the model.

When the description names a single action that is carried out on one branch of a conditional decision, and the description gives that action no ordered sequence of its own steps, only a phrase naming the activity: Model that named action as one bpmn:task on the branch leaving the decision gateway, connected by sequence flow from the gateway and to the next element the description names. Do not wrap it in a bpmn:subProcess with its own start and end events, and do not leave the branch without an activity. Use a subProcess only when the description states an ordered workflow of several steps that belongs to the parent process.

When the description states that a work item may be revised over several review cycles, that each revision is recorded and approved by responsible parties, and that a later step follows once the final approved state is reached: Model each revision made after a review as its own task, followed by a sequence flow into a separate approval task for that revision. Connect the approval task back to the review cycle so that further cycles can follow, and exit the cycle through a gateway that decides whether another cycle is needed. Model the approval of the final state as its own task with a sequence flow to the next stated step, so that no approved outcome lacks an outgoing flow.

When the description names several activities that must all be finished before the process moves on or ends, and it gives no order among them: Model a parallel gateway that splits into those activities as concurrent branches, and a second parallel gateway that joins the branches before the next element or the end event. Do not chain the activities in a fixed sequence, and do not join them with an exclusive gateway.

A follow-up email for feedback is sent directly after confirming the successful delivery.

Receiving returned items.
Inspecting returned items.
Processing a refund or replacement.
